metadata.title: R1: Money and Trust Erosion
metadata.description: The primary post-Citizens United loop. Lifting limits on independent expenditures elevated donor influence, raised perceived corruption, drained trust, depressed participation, weakened broad accountability — and made independent spending even more decisive.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Citizens United Decision (2010)
nodes.description: The 5-4 Supreme Court ruling that lifted limits on independent political spending. Treated as a one-time structural trigger that opens the loop — not a variable that goes up and down.

nodes.label: Independent Political Spending
nodes.description: Total dollars spent on political ads by super PACs, dark-money groups, corporations, and unions.

nodes.label: Large Donor Influence
nodes.description: The weight of wealthy individuals and major PACs in shaping candidates, messages, and policy.

nodes.label: Public Perception of Corruption
nodes.description: Citizens' belief that officials trade favors for money. Perception alone — not just actual corruption — is enough to erode trust.

nodes.label: Trust In Government
nodes.description: The percentage of citizens who say they trust the federal government to do what is right.

nodes.label: Civic Participation
nodes.description: Voting, organizing, contacting officials — the breadth of ordinary citizens involved in democracy.

nodes.label: Broad Democratic Accountability
nodes.description: The degree to which officials must answer to a wide swath of constituents rather than a narrow donor class.

edges.description: The decision lifted limits on independent expenditures, opening the channel.
More independent dollars means more donor leverage over campaigns.
Visible donor influence — even when legal — raises citizens' suspicion that money is buying outcomes.
Believing the system is corrupt drives trust down.
People who trust the system show up to participate in it.
A broad participating public holds officials to account.
When the broad public is engaged, the relative leverage of independent expenditures falls.
